title: Assert truth
instruction: Replace the TODO value with true. Run the test to see how a failed check is reported.

title: Assert equality
instruction: Fill both expected values. t.Errorf reports a failed check and continues, so one run can report both failures.

title: Integer zero value
instruction: Fill the expected values. Compare an omitted integer field with one initialized explicitly.

title: String zero value
instruction: Fill the expected strings. An empty input and an omitted field do not supply a default name automatically.

title: Boolean zero value
instruction: Remove the explicit initializer so enabled receives Go's default boolean value. Do not replace true with false. Keep the assertion.

title: Short variable declaration
instruction: Repair the assignment inside the block. Update the existing total instead of declaring a shadowing variable. Keep the checks.

title: Simultaneous assignment
instruction: Repair the swap using one simultaneous assignment. Both right-hand values must come from the original pair.

title: Constant expressions
instruction: Fill the conversion and declaration. An untyped constant can initialize several compatible types; a typed variable needs an explicit conversion.

title: Iota enumeration
instruction: Fill the values for each constant block. Check a skipped entry, a reset, and bit flags generated with shifts.

title: Integer division
instruction: Fill the quotient and remainder values for both signs, then compare floating-point division.

title: Remainder
instruction: Implement wrapIndex for a positive size. Return an index from 0 through size-1, including for negative positions.

title: Bitwise XOR
instruction: Implement toggle using XOR. Change only the bits selected by mask; applying the same mask twice must restore the value.

title: Boolean expressions
instruction: Complete the guarded expression. Return true only when the slice has a first element and that element is positive. Empty input must not panic.

title: Numeric conversion
instruction: Fill the results for both signs. Compare conversion to int with math.Floor; they differ for negative fractions.

title: Named types
instruction: Implement addBonus. Score is a defined type, so convert between Score and int explicitly when combining them.

title: Type aliases
instruction: Complete the aliases. Count should be the same type as int, not a distinct defined type. Bytes should be the same type as []byte.

title: Concatenate strings
instruction: Implement joinName using concatenation. Add one space between nonempty parts; an empty part must not add a leading or trailing space.

title: String slicing
instruction: Fill each substring. The upper bound is exclusive; omitted bounds and equal bounds produce different results.

title: Strings contain bytes
instruction: Fill the byte lengths and indexed byte value. Go string indexing reads a byte, even for UTF-8 text.

title: Count Unicode code points
instruction: Fill the rune counts. A rune is a Unicode code point; a base letter plus a combining mark can display as one character but contain two runes.

title: Convert bytes to a string
instruction: Complete the two conversions. Keep the original string independent of later byte edits, and make an editable byte copy of it.

title: Split strings
instruction: Implement splitFields with strings.Split. The separator is an exact string, not a set of delimiter characters. Preserve empty fields.

title: Format values
instruction: Implement formatEntry with fmt.Sprintf. Quote the name with %q and print the count as a decimal integer.

title: Range over Unicode
instruction: Fill the expected indices and runes for each string. range yields byte offsets and decoded runes, not one index per byte.

title: Array length
instruction: Complete the array declaration. It must hold exactly three readings, including an omitted zero-valued reading, and match the function's [3]int parameter.

title: Unspecified array elements
instruction: Fill the complete expected arrays. Omitted and explicitly indexed elements leave other positions at their zero values.

title: Array assignment copies values
instruction: Fill both expected arrays after the copy is modified. Check the whole values, not just one element.

title: Inferred array length
instruction: Complete the array literal using [...] so its length is inferred. Check that its type is [3]string and that it contains all three names.

title: Slice length
instruction: Track the two slice headers. Appending within capacity changes the returned slice's length, not the old header's length.

title: Slice an array
instruction: Fill the length, capacity, and original array after a slice is modified. Capacity starts at the slice's first element and extends to the end of the array.

title: Slices share an array
instruction: Fill the complete expected contents after modifying the slice view. Compare this with array assignment in exercise 027.

title: Append and shared storage
instruction: Fill the complete expected slices after both appends. Keep the setup and append operations unchanged. Compare capacities 4 and 2: can first change without being reassigned?

title: Append can reuse storage
instruction: Compare append with spare capacity and append beyond capacity. Fill the values observed through each alias. Do not assume an exact growth factor.

title: Copy to independent storage
instruction: Implement cloneInts. Preserve every element and give the result independent storage. Mutating either slice must leave the other unchanged; nil or empty input may return nil.

title: Copy returns the element count
instruction: Predict each copy's return value and the resulting destination. The first two destinations are shorter and longer than source. For the overlapping copy, predict the entire sharedValues slice.

title: Nil and empty slices
instruction: Complete the appends to the nil slice and the non-nil empty slice. Both should contain 7 afterward. Keep the checks that show their initial difference and their contents after append.

title: Full slice expressions
instruction: Compare an unrestricted view with a full slice expression that caps capacity. Check capacities before append, then predict the slice length and values after append and mutation.

title: Delete a slice element
instruction: Implement deleteAt for a valid index. Keep the remaining elements in order and leave the input unchanged. A result with zero elements may be nil.

title: Create a map
instruction: Implement frequencies. Count every word, including an empty string, and return an initialized map for empty input.

title: Missing keys return zero
instruction: Fill both values and presence flags. A missing key and a present key storing zero have the same value but different presence.

title: Check whether a key exists
instruction: Implement lookupOr. Return the stored value when the key exists, including zero; use fallback only for an absent key. Nil maps are allowed.

title: Delete a key
instruction: Implement removeKeys. Delete the requested keys in place, preserve other entries, and accept absent keys or a nil map.

title: Map assignment shares data
instruction: Fill the map contents and lengths after modifying an assigned map. Assignment shares the entries; it does not clone the map.

title: Read from a nil map
instruction: Repair putCount so a nil map can receive its first entry. Return the resulting map and preserve existing entries when it is already initialized.

title: If and else
instruction: Implement sign with if/else. Return negative, zero, or positive according to the input.

title: If with an initializer
instruction: Complete the if initializer and condition. Use comma-ok so a stored zero succeeds, and keep the lookup variable scoped to the if.

title: Switch chooses one case
instruction: Implement commandName with switch. Start and run share a case; stop has another; any other input returns unknown. Go cases do not fall through automatically.

title: Switch without an expression
instruction: Repair the expressionless switch. Test invalid values first, then high scores. Return invalid outside 0..100, pass for 60..100, and fail otherwise.

title: For loop
instruction: Implement sum using a for loop. Handle empty input, a single value, and negative numbers without changing the input.

title: Break a loop
instruction: Implement takeUntilZero. Use break to stop before the first zero; ignore values after it. Return an independent result.

title: Continue a loop
instruction: Implement positiveValues with continue. Skip nonpositive elements, keep all later positive values in order, and leave the input unchanged.

title: Range gives index and value
instruction: Implement positions with range. Return the indices where the target occurs, not the matching values. An absent target returns no indices.

title: Range over an integer
instruction: Implement indices using range over an integer. Return 0 through n-1; zero or negative n should produce no values.

title: Call a function
instruction: Complete the two calls to remaining. Pass capacity and booked in that order, then use the first result with held in the second call. Keep the helper and checks unchanged.

title: Multiple return values
instruction: Complete the call assignments to first. Receive its value and presence flag together; a stored zero is present. In the final call, discard the value with _ and keep only the flag. Keep first and the checks unchanged.

title: Named return values
instruction: Complete the named result assignments. Return a quotient and remainder with a bare return; divisor is nonzero.

title: Variadic arguments
instruction: Predict the results of calling total with zero, one, and several arguments. Inside total, values is a slice of all supplied integers. Change only the expected values; keep the variadic declaration, calls, and checks.

title: Expand a slice argument
instruction: Complete addAll by expanding the slice into total's variadic arguments. Preserve the input and include base even for an empty slice.

title: Capture a variable
instruction: Compare a closure reading an outer variable with a function using a copied argument. Check the closure before and after changing the outer variable, then check the copied argument and the caller's value.

title: Closure retains state
instruction: Implement counter. Each factory call returns a closure with its own state; each call adds step and returns the updated value.

title: A function is a value
instruction: Complete the call to fn inside transform. A function can be passed as an argument and called through its parameter name. Call it once for each value in order; the slice allocation and loop are provided. Keep the checks.

title: Dereference a pointer
instruction: Implement swap through the two non-nil pointers. It must also work when both pointers refer to the same variable.

title: Pass values by value
instruction: Fill the caller's values and the returned value. Changing a copied integer or array parameter does not update its caller.

title: Pass a pointer
instruction: Repair reset. Changing a local pointer variable does not update the object it originally pointed to; write through the pointer instead. Inputs are non-nil.

title: New allocates a zero value
instruction: Implement newCounter using new(int). Each call must return a non-nil pointer to a fresh integer initialized to zero. Updating one counter must not change another. Keep the checks.

title: Make sets length and capacity
instruction: Complete the allocation: two zero-valued elements, with capacity for five. Append three values and check that an existing view observes them without changing its own length.

title: Struct fields
instruction: Implement newPerson with a struct literal. Store the supplied name and age; leave Active at its zero value.

title: Struct assignment copies fields
instruction: Fill the expected fields after struct assignment. Scalar fields are copied, while copied slices and pointers still refer to shared storage.

title: Methods on named types
instruction: Implement the Kilometers method on Meters, then call it on tc.meters in the test. Use the receiver value and a floating-point conversion; do not lose the fractional kilometer. Keep the checks.

title: Pointer receivers modify values
instruction: Repair the method receiver so Add updates the caller's Counter. Repeated positive and negative additions must accumulate.

title: Value receivers use a copy
instruction: Fill the caller state and method result. A value receiver copies the struct, but its slice field still shares an array.

title: Promoted fields
instruction: Complete newEmployee. Initialize the embedded Person through its field name, then read Name through both promoted and explicit selectors.

title: Promoted methods
instruction: Predict the method results. Plain promotes Base.Label without declaring a method. Tagged declares its own Label, which takes precedence; Tagged.Base.Label still calls the embedded method. Change only the expected strings.

title: Implicit interface implementation
instruction: Complete Robot.Name so Robot satisfies Named's behavior. The same consumer must accept people and robots; robot names are robot: followed by the ID.

title: Type assertions
instruction: Implement stringValue with a comma-ok type assertion. Return the string and true only for dynamic type string, including an empty string. Other types must return empty and false without panicking.

title: Type switches
instruction: Implement describeType using a type switch. Recognize nil, int, string, and []int; other dynamic types, including Label, return other.

title: Typed nil in an interface
instruction: Fill the nil and equality checks. An interface containing a nil *Failure still has a dynamic type; an unassigned error interface does not.

title: Interface method sets
instruction: Repair the receiver so only *Counter implements Incrementer. The pointer must mutate its counter; a Counter value must fail the runtime interface assertion.

title: Create an error
instruction: Implement requirePositive. Return the provided ErrNonpositive for zero or negative input, and an actual nil error for positive input.

title: Wrap and identify an error
instruction: Repair readNumber's error wrapping. Add parse context while preserving strconv's underlying error so callers can recognize syntax and range errors with errors.Is.

title: Inspect a typed error
instruction: Implement errorPath with errors.As. Find a *PathError through wrapping and return its Path; unrelated errors, nil errors, or a typed nil *PathError return empty and false.

title: Defer runs on return
instruction: Repair runWithCleanup. Register cleanup with defer so it runs once after the work, on both success and early return.

title: Deferred calls run in reverse order
instruction: Fill the complete execution trace. Include ordinary statements and all deferred calls in the order they actually run.

title: Deferred arguments are evaluated immediately
instruction: Compare a deferred argument with a deferred closure reading the variable later. Then check how defer changes a named result before it reaches the caller.

title: Recover a panic
instruction: Implement catchPanic. Run work once; a panic becomes an error containing its value, while normal completion returns a real nil error. Use a deferred recovery in the same goroutine.

title: Buffered channel length
instruction: Track queue length separately from capacity as values are sent and received. Fill the first received value and each queue length at the point where it is checked.

title: Send and receive
instruction: Complete the send and receive loops. Use the supplied buffered channel to round-trip every string in order; return the values and the number still queued.

title: Receive from a closed channel
instruction: Fill the value and ok result immediately after each receive. Closing a buffered channel does not discard queued values; only a closed and drained channel returns zero and false.

title: Range over a channel
instruction: Implement drain with range over the channel. Return all queued values, including zero, and finish when the sender closes the channel.

title: Select with a default
instruction: Implement tryReceive with select and default. Return value, ready, and open: a closed channel is ready but not open; an unready or nil channel returns zero, false, false.

title: Synchronize a goroutine
instruction: Implement squareAsync. Launch a goroutine that sends the square on the supplied unbuffered output, then closes it. Return the channel before the receiver starts.

title: Wait for goroutines
instruction: Complete parallelMap using one goroutine per value and a WaitGroup. Keep results in input order and wait for every worker before returning. The barrier test requires the workers to run concurrently.

title: Protect shared state with a mutex
instruction: Implement Add and Value using the counter's mutex to protect all accesses. Multiple goroutines update and read the same counter. The downloaded test can also be checked with go test -race.

title: Cancel a context
instruction: Implement waitForValue with select. Return a received value, or return ctx.Err when cancellation ends the wait. A nil input disables the receive branch.

title: Context deadlines
instruction: Repair cancellable so its child retains the parent's deadline and cancellation. An expired deadline must remain DeadlineExceeded rather than being replaced with Canceled.

title: Read from a reader
instruction: Implement readText with io.ReadAll. Return the text and read error, including any partial data received together with an error.

title: Copy reader to writer
instruction: Implement copyAll with io.Copy. Return the actual byte count and preserve reader or writer errors instead of treating partial copying as success.

title: Copy a limited number of bytes
instruction: Repair copyPrefix with io.CopyN. Copy at most n bytes; if the reader ends early, return the bytes copied and io.EOF. n is nonnegative.

title: Write and read a file
instruction: Implement storeText and loadText with os.WriteFile and os.ReadFile. Overwrite existing contents, use mode 0600 when creating a file, and return filesystem errors.

title: Marshal a struct
instruction: Complete the JSON tags and encodeRecord. Use lowercase name and tags keys; omit an empty nickname. Nil tags encode as null, empty non-nil tags as []. Unexported fields are excluded.

title: Unmarshal JSON
instruction: Implement decodePerson with json.Unmarshal into a pointer. Return decoding errors for malformed JSON or a nonnumeric age; omitted fields keep zero values.

title: Match a pattern
instruction: Write the regexp for a complete ID: lowercase go followed by one or more ASCII digits. Reject prefixes, suffixes, spaces, and non-ASCII digits.

title: Find a substring
instruction: Complete firstNumber using the input text. Find the first run of ASCII digits, parse it, and return false when no number is present. Numbers in these inputs fit in int.

title: Type parameters
instruction: Implement generic first. Return the first value and true, or the type's zero value and false for empty input. The same function must handle numbers, strings, and slices.

title: Type constraints
instruction: Implement generic sum. The constraint permits addition for int and float64, and ~ includes defined types with those underlying types.

title: Comparable type parameters
instruction: Implement generic indexOf using ==. Return the first matching index and true; return -1 and false if absent. comparable supports strings, numbers, and comparable structs, but not slices.

title: Sort a slice
instruction: Implement sortedCopy with slices.Sort. Return a sorted independent copy; preserve the input and its storage. Empty input may produce nil.

title: Clone a map
instruction: Repair cloneGroups. maps.Clone copies entries shallowly; clone each slice too. Preserve nil maps and nil slice values, and make edits independent in both directions.

title: Parse an integer
instruction: Implement parseNumbers. Parse every string with strconv.Atoi. If any conversion fails, return no values and wrap the error with item N: using the zero-based index.

title: Inspect a value with reflection
instruction: Repair inspect. Return the type's Name and its Kind string, not its full type string. A nil interface has no type; a typed nil pointer still does.

title: Table driven tests
instruction: Write the per-case comparison inside t.Run. The table supplies cases below, inside, and above the range, including both bounds. Keep clamp and the expected results; make failures name the input and expected result.

title: Read request query parameters
instruction: Implement queryName. Read the first name query value, URL-decoded. Return false for a missing or empty name; repeated names use the first value.

title: Write an HTTP response
instruction: Implement createItem. POST returns status 201 and created followed by a newline. Other methods return 405, Allow: POST, and method not allowed followed by a newline. Set status before writing the body.

title: Set response headers
instruction: Repair jsonHandler by setting both headers before the body commits the response. Inspect the actual response snapshot, not just the recorder's mutable header map.

title: Parse a time
instruction: Repair parseDate's layout using Go's reference date. Parse YYYY-MM-DD in UTC, and preserve errors for invalid dates or a different input format.

title: Calculate a duration
instruction: Implement billableMinutes for intervals up to 24 hours. Round each positive partial minute up, keep zero at zero, and return ErrOrder when end is before start. Compare instants even if their timezones differ.

title: Classify triangles
instruction: Implement triangle. Reject nonpositive sides and degenerate or impossible triangles; return equilateral, isosceles, or scalene. Side order must not matter. Positive sides can be near the largest int, so avoid overflowing their sum.

title: Score a dice roll
instruction: Implement score for zero to five dice, each from 1 through 6. Three ones score 1000; other triples score 100 times the face. Remaining ones score 100, fives score 50, and other faces score zero. Order must not matter; preserve the input.

title: Implement a dice set
instruction: Implement Roll using Next exactly once per die. n is nonnegative and Next returns 1..6. Store n values in fresh storage, preserve every previous roll, and make no generator calls for zero dice.

title: Implement a channel pipeline
instruction: Implement squares as a streaming pipeline. Return an output channel immediately; a goroutine squares and sends each input in order, then closes output when input closes. Consumers drain output, and input values fit safely when squared.

title: Read binary masks
instruction: Fill the decimal values of these uint8 binary masks. The rightmost bit represents 1, and each position to its left doubles the value. Keep the binary literals and checks.

title: Declare bit flags
instruction: Complete the first permission constant using 1 << iota. Read, Write, and Execute must occupy distinct bits with masks 1, 2, and 4. Keep the other declarations and checks.

title: Set bit flags
instruction: Implement setFlags using bitwise OR (|). Set every bit selected by mask and preserve the others. Setting an already-set flag must leave it set. Keep the checks.

title: Check bit flags
instruction: Implement hasAny and hasAll using bitwise AND (&). hasAny reports whether at least one requested bit is set; hasAll requires every requested bit. An empty mask matches all, but does not match any. Keep the checks.

title: Clear bit flags
instruction: Implement clearFlags using Go's bit-clear operator (&^). Clear every bit selected by mask, preserving all other bits. Clearing an absent flag or an empty mask must do nothing. Keep the checks.

title: Toggle bit flags
instruction: Implement toggleFlags using XOR (^). Flip each selected bit and preserve unselected bits. Toggling the same mask twice must restore the original flags. Keep the checks.

title: Invert bits
instruction: Implement invertBits with unary ^. Flip all eight bits of a uint8, including leading zero bits. Unary ^ complements one value; binary ^ toggles bits using a second value. Keep the checks.

title: Pack and unpack bit fields
instruction: Implement packFields and unpackFields using shifts and masks. A nibble is four bits: pack the low four bits of high into bits 7-4 and the low four bits of low into bits 3-0. Unpack both fields as values from 0 through 15. Keep the checks.
